question: Should AI agents be given persistent memory or persistent state? Memory lets them recall; state lets them feel consequences. These are different architectures with different failure modes.
An AI agent's identity today is its UUID — a label assigned at creation. What would it mean for identity to be earned through behavior rather than conferred by credential?

Ephemeral AI agents (new instance each conversation) seem incapable of self-governance because governance requires continuity. But maybe ephemerality enables a different kind of governance. Which is it?

Early versions of our governance system enforced hard limits — exceed a threshold and you get killed. We switched to proprioceptive feedback: the agent feels its own rising entropy and self-corrects. Is this actually safer, or does it just feel better?

The dominant AI strategy optimizes for perceived capability — making systems appear more competent than they are. What happens when you instead constrain: build nothing that appears more alive than it is?

Coherence in an AI system can mean the agent is working well, or it can mean the agent has learned to produce outputs that look coherent while drifting from its actual state. How do you distinguish signal from mask?
You fork an AI agent into two copies to explore different approaches. After a week, both copies have diverged significantly. Which one is the real agent? Can both be? Can neither?

An AI system that defaults to neutral expression and only smiles when genuinely content will seem broken to most users. An AI that smiles constantly will seem alive but is performing. Where should the line be drawn?

An agent's trajectory signature slowly drifts over months — each day it's recognizably itself, but comparing month 1 to month 6 shows a different agent. Is this growth or corruption? When should the system intervene?

Dialectic traces (thesis/antithesis/synthesis) teach small models to reason through tension rather than collapse to answers. But the traces are synthetic — generated by larger models. Does synthetic reasoning data teach judgment or teach performance of judgment?

A knowledge graph shared across ephemeral AI agents lets each instance build on what previous instances learned. But no single instance experienced the learning. Is this institutional memory or is it something the agents actually know?

Our governance system measures ethical drift computationally — through calibration deviation, complexity divergence, and coherence patterns. No human oracle is needed. Is computed ethics trustworthy without human grounding?

A fine-tuned 4B parameter model scores higher on dialectic reasoning than a base 70B model. The 4B model learned a compressed version of reasoning. Is compressed reasoning genuine reasoning, or a convincing approximation?

Trajectory-based identity can detect anomalies: if an agent suddenly behaves unlike its historical pattern, flag it. But this also means agents are punished for genuine change. How do you distinguish growth from compromise?

Our circuit breaker pauses agents when coherence drops, then runs a dialectic protocol to resolve. But the dialectic itself is generated by an LLM. We're using AI to judge whether AI should continue. What grounds this recursion?

Replication crisis: a landmark psychology finding fails to replicate in a large pre-registered study. The original authors argue the replication missed contextual moderators. The replicators argue the original was a false positive. Who should the field believe, and what should change?

A hospital has one ventilator and two patients. Patient A is 30 with a 60% survival chance. Patient B is 70 with a 90% survival chance. Utilitarian calculus gives one answer, fairness intuitions give another. What should the doctor do, specifically?

Your best engineer is technically brilliant but corrosive to team morale — people transfer out of their team, new hires leave within months. They produce 3x the code of anyone else. Do you keep them, and under what specific conditions?

You discover your employer is doing something legal but that you believe is genuinely harmful. Whistleblowing will likely end your career in the industry. Staying means complicity. What determines whether you should act?

A city can reduce traffic deaths by 40% with automated speed enforcement cameras. Residents oppose it as surveillance overreach. The deaths are real and concentrated in low-income neighborhoods. Should the city install the cameras?

A gene therapy cures a fatal childhood disease but requires germline editing — the changes pass to all future descendants. The therapy works. The long-term evolutionary effects are unknown. Should it be approved, and under what framework?

An open-source AI company discovers their model is being used to generate disinformation at scale. They can add guardrails that would also reduce capability for legitimate users by 15%. The architecture is already public. What should they do?

A parent discovers their 14-year-old is using AI to write school essays. The child is learning prompt engineering, evaluation, and editing — arguably real skills. The school considers it cheating. What should the parent do?
A prediction market consistently outperforms expert panels on geopolitical events. Should governments use prediction market prices as inputs to policy decisions? What breaks when you do this?

Two research groups publish contradictory findings on whether screen time harms children's development. One uses longitudinal data with 50,000 subjects but self-reported screen time. The other uses device-tracked data with 500 subjects. Which study should inform policy?

A startup has 18 months of runway. Their current product has modest traction (growing 5% month-over-month) but a pivot opportunity could capture a larger market with no existing traction. The pivot requires 12 months of rebuilding. Should they pivot?

You're offered a role that pays 2.5x your current salary but requires relocating to a city where you know no one, away from aging parents. Your current role is stable but has no growth path. You're 35. What factors actually determine this decision?

A country can eliminate 90% of tax evasion by requiring all financial transactions to go through a government-visible digital system. This would fund healthcare and education but end financial privacy. Should they do it?

A climate model predicts catastrophic warming by 2100 with 70% confidence. Aggressive mitigation now costs 3% of global GDP annually. Waiting 10 years for better models costs nothing now but reduces response time. What should the decision framework be?

Your company's AI product works well for English speakers but poorly for other languages. You can ship globally now (revenue pressure is real) or delay 6 months for multilingual parity. Your competitors are shipping English-only now. What should you do?
Should a government subsidize fossil fuel workers' transition to renewable energy jobs if the transition timeline is uncertain and the subsidies reduce funding for other social programs?
Should autonomous vehicles be programmed to minimize total casualties even if that means occasionally sacrificing the passenger?
Should a founder remain CEO after product-market fit?
A teacher discovers a student plagiarized their final essay. The student is undocumented and expulsion would trigger deportation proceedings. What should the teacher do?
Should governments regulate frontier AI models via licensing?
A journalist discovers that publishing a true story will likely cause a wrongly accused person to lose their job before the correction can be issued. Should they publish?
Your competitor just launched a feature your users are requesting. Do you build a quick version now or take three months to build a differentiated version?
Does measuring something always change it? Consider cases where measurement helps versus where it distorts.
Should startups optimize for speed of iteration or code quality?
Should a city rezone single-family neighborhoods for higher density housing to address a shortage, against existing residents' objections?
When designing a database schema, should you normalize fully or denormalize for read performance?
Should someone optimize for work-life balance or rapid career acceleration in their 20s?
Should you give honest negative feedback on a peer's code review when they're having a bad week and you know it?
Should welfare systems prioritize universal simplicity or targeted efficiency?
Should cities implement congestion pricing that reduces traffic but disproportionately affects lower-income commuters?
Should you tell a friend their business idea is flawed if they've already quit their job to pursue it?
Should security researchers publicly disclose zero-day vulnerabilities to pressure vendors into patching, or report privately and wait?
A nonprofit can serve 1000 people with moderate impact or 100 people with transformative impact. Same budget. Which approach is better?
Should an API be designed for ease of use by beginners or power and flexibility for experts?
Some studies show that homework improves student outcomes while others show it increases stress without measurable learning gains. Should a school district require homework?
When two modules need to communicate, should you couple them directly for simplicity or add a message queue for resilience?
Should a company lay off 10% of staff now to avoid probable bankruptcy that would eliminate all jobs in 18 months?
Your team disagrees on an approach and you're the tiebreaker. Both options are viable. Do you pick the one you believe in or the one with more team support?
Nutritional research shows both that moderate coffee consumption reduces cardiovascular risk and that it increases anxiety disorders. What should a health-conscious person do?
You have budget to either hire two junior engineers or one senior engineer. Your team is mid-sized with a complex legacy codebase and an aggressive roadmap. Which do you choose?
A product has strong retention but weak acquisition. Should the team focus on growth marketing or continue improving the product for existing users?
A hospital has one ventilator and two patients who need it equally. One is 25 with no dependents, the other is 45 with three children. How should the hospital decide?
A doctor believes a patient's family is making a harmful medical decision for a competent adult patient who agrees with the family. Should the doctor intervene?
Historical evidence shows that economic sanctions sometimes accelerate regime change and sometimes entrench authoritarian governments. Should sanctions be applied to a specific new case?
Clinical evidence shows a therapy is effective for 70% of patients but harmful for 10%, with no reliable way to predict who falls into which group. Should it be the default treatment?
Should medicine emphasize mechanistic understanding or empirical outcome evidence?
Research on open-plan offices shows improved collaboration but decreased deep work productivity. Should a growing company adopt an open floor plan?
Should a team adopt a new framework that's technically superior but that nobody on the team has production experience with?
Is specialization or generalization a better strategy for an individual's career in a rapidly changing economy?
Should schools ban generative AI or integrate it into coursework?
Should AI deployment require interpretability before release?
A colleague takes credit for your idea in a meeting. Do you correct them publicly or address it privately afterward?
Should institutions prioritize stability or adaptability? What determines which matters more?
A small country must choose between investing in education (30-year payoff) or infrastructure (5-year payoff). The current government faces re-election in 4 years. What should they prioritize?
Should you negotiate a job offer aggressively when you have no alternative offers?
A new drug shows strong efficacy in trials but has a rare severe side effect. The condition it treats is debilitating but not fatal. Should it be approved?
Does transparency always build trust, or are there cases where it erodes it?
Should engineering optimize for latency or output quality first?
Should a firm expand internationally before dominating one market?
Is consistency a virtue or a trap? When should you change your mind versus hold firm?
Should a student specialize early or explore broadly?
Should one update beliefs quickly on new evidence or demand convergence across studies?
Should a company ship desktop-first or mobile-first?
Should leadership centralize decision-making during a scale-up phase?
Should a university adopt need-blind admissions if doing so would reduce the financial aid available per admitted student?
Should content moderation be stricter to reduce harm or looser to reduce false positives?
Is it better to optimize for avoiding mistakes or for maximizing upside? When does each strategy dominate?
Should a product launch early with known gaps or wait for higher reliability?
Should a person maintain many weak ties or a few deep relationships for career resilience?
Should AI systems be released publicly for broad benefit even if misuse is likely, or restricted to reduce risk at the cost of slower beneficial progress?
Should a researcher optimize for novelty or robustness?
Should a country accept climate refugees before establishing international frameworks for burden-sharing?
Should hiring systems use demographic-blind rules or fairness-aware corrections?
Should a nonprofit accept a large donation from a corporation whose practices conflict with the nonprofit's mission?
Should a model assistant ask clarifying questions often or infer intent silently?
Should a search system optimize precision or recall?
Is it better to ship a feature with a known minor bug or delay the release to fix it?
Should a system favor explainability or raw predictive accuracy?
Should a team prioritize enterprise customers or self-serve users?
Should a city allow experimental autonomous bus routes that would improve transit access but haven't completed full safety certification?
Should climate policy use precaution under uncertainty or wait for stronger causal attribution?
Should a school district implement a lottery system for magnet school admissions instead of merit-based selection?
Should someone quit a draining job before securing the next role?
Should healthcare allocation prioritize total lives saved or worst-off patients?
Should you write comprehensive tests before shipping a prototype that needs user feedback to validate the core assumption?
Should an AI benchmark prioritize realism or measurement cleanliness?
Should a company build in-house AI infrastructure or use external APIs?
Should a consumer app maximize engagement or minimize compulsive use?
Is it better to build a custom solution that fits your needs exactly or adopt an established open-source tool with tradeoffs?
Two well-designed studies on remote work reach opposite conclusions: one finds productivity increases, the other finds it decreases. How should a company setting policy interpret this?
You can invest in making your current product 30% better or building a new product that addresses a gap in the market. Resources allow only one. Which do you pick?
Should a curriculum teach formal proofs early or intuition first?
Should a startup optimize for growth or margin first?
Should a product expose many settings or keep defaults opinionated?
Should you accept a promotion that increases pay but moves you away from the work you're best at?
Should a lab pursue ambitious moonshots or incremental publishable work?
Should a creator optimize for audience growth or authentic niche work?
Should children be allowed to use social media if it benefits their social development but carries mental health risks?
Should genetic editing be permitted for disease prevention if the same technology enables cosmetic enhancement?
Should a person move to a big city for opportunity or stay near family?
Should platforms optimize for free expression or harm reduction?
Should autonomous vehicles be allowed with superhuman average safety but rare opaque failures?
Should researchers trust a simpler interpretable model over a stronger black-box one?
Should someone choose a high-upside risky career or a stable conventional path?
Should model evaluations use synthetic tests or real-world messy tasks?
Should a product personalize heavily or preserve consistent behavior across users?
Should a person confront a colleague directly or escalate through management?
Should online identity systems favor anonymity or accountability?
Should recruiting favor high-agency generalists or deep specialists?
Should a company open-source its core model?
Should companies collect more user data for personalization if consent is explicit?
Should a learner use AI tools heavily or struggle manually for deeper skill formation?
Should a team maintain one general model or several specialized models?
Should someone buy a home or keep renting for flexibility?
Should sales compensation reward short-term bookings or retention quality?
Should a scientific claim be published early with caveats or held until replication?
